learned-level-generation technique sourced

Learned level and map generation (PCGRL, MarioGPT, LLM generators)

Generators trained by reinforcement learning or on example levels, including small and large language models that emit tile maps from text prompts, produce playable levels and maps without hand-written generation rules.

Procedural content generation2023Researchdeterminism Mitigable4 mechanics affected
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

mechanism

PCGRL treats level design as a sequential decision problem: an agent edits a tile grid step by step (narrow, turtle, or wide representations of where it may edit) and is rewarded by the change in a quality score such as playability, path length, or region count, so the trained generator builds a level in fast forward passes without example levels. ARLPCG adds a solver agent and rewards the generator for levels that are challenging but solvable, with auxiliary control inputs. Language-model generators serialize levels as text and train or prompt a model to continue them: MarioGPT fine-tunes DistilGPT2 with cross-attention to a prompt naming pipes, enemies, blocks, and elevation; Sokoban generators fine-tune on level corpora; Word2World prompts a general LLM to write a story, extract characters and tiles, and place them. Outputs are checked by search agents or solver bots and rejected or repaired if unplayable. Conditional generators such as EA SEED's match-3 cVAE take size, symmetry, and target difficulty as inputs.

limitations

  • Example data is scarce: MarioGPT trained on 37 levels and LLM Sokoban results scaled with dataset size, so a new game's handful of authored maps may not suffice.
  • Validity is not guaranteed: about 12% of MarioGPT levels were not completed by an A* agent, so every output needs a solver check.
  • Conditional control is weak: difficulty conditioning hit its target a third of the time and lowered size and tile-distribution accuracy.
  • Results are mostly 2D tile grids for small games; large simulation maps with resources, rivers, and settlement suitability carry global constraints these models do not represent.
  • Training on existing commercial levels such as Super Mario Bros raises IP and platform disclosure questions for shipped use.

relations

4 stored edges
affects

Adaptive threat scaling

Difficulty-conditioned generators let the next map or wave be built at a target difficulty instead of multiplying enemy counts, though EA SEED's match-3 model hit the requested difficulty only a third of the time.

Deepens
affects

Generative content on demand

Text-to-level models small enough to run on the client (MarioGPT has 96M parameters) let players request maps in words at runtime, extending generated content from text and items to playable space.

Deepens
affects

Procedural terrain

Hand-written noise and placement rules give way to a generator trained on example maps or prompted with text, so a seed becomes a prompt plus a sample, and validity must be checked by a solver instead of guaranteed by construction.

Replaces substrate
affects

Scenario objectives

Scenario maps can be produced from a written description of the situation, Word2World-style story to world, with an agent playthrough confirming the stated goal is reachable.

Cuts authoring cost

claims

6 with sources
c01high

PCGRL (2020) framed level design as a Markov decision process with three editing representations tested on three games, giving a fast generator that needs few or no example levels.

src-khalifa-2020-pcgrl

c02high

MarioGPT (2023) fine-tuned a 96M-parameter DistilGPT2 model on 37 Super Mario Bros levels; 88.4% of 250 generated levels were completed by an A* agent versus about 31% for an LSTM baseline, and output followed text prompts.

src-sudhakaran-2023-mariogpt

c03high

LLM Sokoban level generation improved sharply with training-set size, and scarce level data was the main obstacle (FDG 2023).

src-todd-2023-llm-level-generation

c04medium

Word2World (2024) used off-the-shelf LLMs without fine-tuning to write a story and place tiles into a coherent, playable 2D world.

src-nasir-2024-word2world

c05high

EA SEED's difficulty-conditioned match-3 generator produced 51.39% valid levels versus 46.15% in its training data, but matched the requested difficulty only 33.33% of the time (mean gap 10.19 moves).

src-villanueva-2024-match3-conditional-generation

c06medium

ARLPCG trained a generator adversarially against a solver agent in a 3D platformer and a racing game, producing new environments shown to be solvable.

src-gisslen-2021-arlpcg
